chunks: And it was narrated from Ādam ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Juʿfī, who said:

I was with Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and a letter from Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came to him regarding a man who had exhumed a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and had intercourse with her. The people here had differed before us: one group said, "Kill him," and another group said, "Burn him."

So he عليه السلام wrote back to him: "The sanctity of the deceased is like the sanctity of the living. His punishment is that his hand be cut off for his grave-exhumation and stripping of the clothes, and the hadd punishment for zina is to be carried out upon him. If he was muḥṣan, he is to be stoned, and if he was not muḥṣan, he is to be flogged one hundred lashes."

key_terms.أُحْصِنَ: being muḥṣan, legally protected through valid marriage
key_terms.الْحَدُّ فِي الزِّنَا: the prescribed legal punishment for zina
key_terms.حُرْمَةَ الْمَيِّتِ: the inviolable sanctity of the deceased
key_terms.سَلْبِهِ الثِّيَابَ: stripping and taking the clothing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who exhumes a grave, steals from the deceased, and commits zina with a corpse in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a man who violated the grave of a woman, stole her clothing, and committed intercourse with her corpse. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that the sanctity of the deceased is like that of the living, and he assigns separate punishments for grave violation and theft, and for zina according to the offender's muḥṣan status.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5145 - It was narrated from Adam ibn Ishaq from Abdullah ibn Muhammad Al-Jufi who said:

I was with Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) when a letter from Hisham ibn Abd Al-Malik arrived regarding a man who had exhumed the grave of a woman, stolen her clothes, and committed intercourse with her. The people were divided on how to punish him: some said: "Kill him," while others said: "Burn him."

Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) wrote back to him:
"The sanctity of the deceased is like the sanctity of the living. His punishment is that his hand should be cut off for exhuming the grave and stealing the clothing, and the legal punishment for adultery is to be applied to him.
If he was married (muhsan), he is to be stoned, and if he was not married, he is to be flogged one hundred lashes."
